backstory:
Brother Hessek has spent his life bent over a copying desk, ruling lines by lamplight and rendering the Aurulent Tome in a hand so even the Syrinx archivists no longer pretend to find fault with it. He is a temple scribe first and a lay cleric second, though in Feyador the two are scarcely separable: to keep the books of Tanagaar is to keep his watch.

He was born in the lower cloisters to a pair of indentured copyists, human hands owned in all but name by the diocese, and he learned his letters before he learned that letters were the one thing that might someday buy a human out from under a Strix overseer. His mother died still owing for the ink she had spilled; his father simply grew old at the desk beside him. Hessek inherited their stool, their debt, and their patient, downcast diligence.

Feyador taught him where a human's ambitions may safely end, and faith taught him to be grateful for the small high window above his desk. He keeps the night-offices without being asked, watches far more than he speaks, and trusts the slow justice of the ledger over the fast justice of men.

Personality: devout, watchful, outwardly meek.
Mannerisms: speaks softly, blots his nib twice before answering a question.
Appearance: ink-stained fingers, a scholar's stoop, a tonsure going early to grey.
Flaws: cannot forgive a debt, least of all his own.
